studies.Reference: Association of Artificially Sweetened Beverage Consumption and Urinary Tract Cancers in the Women's Health Initiative Observational Study.
studies.Title: Association of Artificially Sweetened Beverage Consumption and Urinary Tract Cancers in the Women's Health Initiative Observational Study.
studies.Authors: Ringel NE, Hovey KM, Andrews CA, Mossavar-Rahmani Y, Shadyab AH, Snetselaar LG, Howard BV, Iglesia CB
studies.Population: Postmenopausal women enrolled in the Women's Health Initiative Observational Study (WHI-OS)

sample_size.excerpt: In this secondary analysis of the Women’s Health Initiative Observational Study that included 80 388 postmenopausal women, higher consumption of artificially sweetened beverages was associated with a higher risk of kidney cancer.

effect_size.excerpt: The association between ASB consumption and incidence of ureter and other urinary organ cancers was not assessed due to small numbers of participants in each group. design.excerpt: This was a secondary analysis of data from the Women’s Health Initiative Observational Study, a multicenter longitudinal prospective study of the health of 93 676 postmenopausal women with a mean follow-up time of 13.5 yr.

timing.excerpt: The WHI-OS is a prospective, multicenter cohort study of 93 676 postmenopausal women.

continent.excerpt: Women were identified at 40 clinical centers across the USA and enrolled from 1993 to 1998.

exposure_measurement.excerpt: The question regarding ASBs was as follows: “During the past 3 mo, how often did you drink these beverages?” (Beverages refer to “diet drinks such as Diet Coke or diet fruit drinks,” with a 12 fl. oz. can as a reference serving size.)

studies.Reference: Artificial sweeteners and lower urinary tract cancer: hospital vs. population controls.
studies.Title: Artificial sweeteners and lower urinary tract cancer: hospital vs. population controls.
studies.Authors: Silverman DT, Hoover RN, Swanson GM
studies.Population: Detroit residents enrolled in the National Bladder Cancer Study
studies.comparison_type: Ever use of artificial sweeteners vs never use (males, non-obesity-related hospital controls/population controls)

sample_size.excerpt: The study was based on interviews with 305 hospital controls and 440 population controls, as well as 391 patients with transitional or squamous cell carcinoma of the lower urinary tract.
sample_size.location: abstract; total_n derived from reported group counts 305 + 440 + 391 = 1136

cases.excerpt: In a case-control study conducted in 1978 in Detroit, Michigan, as part of the National Bladder Cancer Study, the proportions of artificial sweetener users in a hospital and a population control series were compared. The study was based on interviews with 305 hospital controls and 440 population controls, as well as 391 patients with transitional or squamous cell carcinoma of the lower urinary tract.

effect_size.excerpt: When controls hospitalized for obesity-related diseases were excluded from the hospital control group, the proportion of artificial sweetener users and the relative risks for males were identical to those estimated with population controls (relative risk = 1.1).

comparison.excerpt: it was found that 44% had ever used artificial sweeteners, compared to 38% of the male population controls

studies.Title: Associations between bladder cancer risk factors and tumor stage and grade at diagnosis.
studies.Authors: Sturgeon SR, Hartge P, Silverman DT, Kantor AF, Linehan WM, Lynch C, Hoover RN
studies.comparison_type: heavy artificial sweetener use versus lower or no use

sample_size.excerpt: Using data on 1,860 bladder cancer cases and 3,934 population-based controls from the National Bladder Cancer Study, we examined associations between suspected bladder cancer risk factors and tumor stage and grade.
sample_size.location: Abstract; total_n derived from reported group counts 1860 + 3934 = 5794

cases.excerpt: Using data on 1,860 bladder cancer cases and 3,934 population-based controls from the National Bladder Cancer Study, we examined associations between suspected bladder cancer risk factors and tumor stage and grade.
